Hi Jordan / Marissa,

Attaching the CSV export from the internal benchmark run: we used an LLM similar to the "rwd-3b" public variant, running on A100-40GB (single GPU) with single-stream inference. Batch sizes: 1 / 4 / 8 were tested. Key notes below: 

- GPU: NVIDIA A100-40GB, single-stream optimized kernel.
- Batch sizes & p95 (short ~300 tokens):
  • batch=1 -> p95 = 78 ms
  • batch=4 -> p95 = 95 ms
  • batch=8 -> p95 = 160 ms
- For long contexts (1k tokens): p95 increases by ~2.8x compared to 300-token runs (cold cache); warm KV cache reduces that by ~20–30% depending on request overlap.
- For 2k tokens: p95 ~ 3.8x of the short-run baseline (cold).
- INT8 quantization: model-size reduced, throughput improves ~1.6x, but p95 for tail cases can be +10–15 ms due to extra dequant/quant overhead on certain ops; qualitative: still within target for many workloads but depends on strict 100ms p95 requirement.

See attached: redwood-latency-report-2026-02-27.csv (raw sample runs) and a short table exported to the PDF Marissa sent earlier.

Let me know if you want a custom run with your exact prompt shapes — we can queue a quick benchmark on a dedicated GPU.

Thanks,
